days.label: OFF DAYS
days.notes: All of this is optional and capped on purpose. It exists to support recovery and the golf swing — not to compete with Thursday's deadlift for the same recovery.

items.name: Bike — Steady State
items.note: Conversational pace · Nasal breathing if you can hold it · Stationary or road, flat to rolling · Should feel easier at the end than at the start

items.name: Jump Rope — Steady State
items.note: Easy pace · Nasal breathing only · Not a conditioning session

items.name: Bike — Intervals
items.note: ~20 min with warm-up and cool-down · Hard enough that talking is difficult, not all-out · Seated against real resistance beats spinning out against none

items.name: Jump Rope — Intervals
items.note: Total ~10 min · Push pace on work intervals · Walk or slow spin on rest

items.name: Conditioning
items.note: Not the day before Thursday

items.name: Full Rest
items.note: Full rest means full rest. Mobility is not mandatory. Sleep is.

days.label: PULL
days.notes: Deadlift leads the week on the freshest day — it carries the most collateral of anything here and shouldn't run on accumulated fatigue. Everything after it is chest-supported or cable-based so the spine stops paying for back work.

items.name: Dead Hang
items.note: Sagittal · Lat in full stretch · Decompress the spine before loading the hinge

items.name: Prone Y Raise
items.note: Frontal · Lower trap and scapular upward rotation · Bodyweight only

items.name: Prone T Raise
items.note: Transverse · Rear delt and external rotators · Warm-up runs the plane hierarchy simple → complex, then ramp sets into Deadlift

items.name: Conventional Deadlift
items.note: 3 min rest · Full recovery between sets · Highest collateral cost in the program, which is why it gets the freshest day

items.name: Weighted Pull-Up or Lat Pulldown
items.note: 2 min rest · Vertical pull · Load the pattern here, isolate the lat later

items.name: Chest-Supported DB or Machine Row
items.note: 2 min rest · Chest support strips the spinal shear out after deadlift — same row stimulus, far less collateral

items.name: Single-Arm Cable Pulldown
items.note: 60 sec rest · Gets to the lat in isolation faster than a bilateral pulldown · Cable holds tension at full overhead stretch, where a free weight goes light

items.name: Reverse Pec Deck
items.note: 60 sec rest · Cam holds tension through the arc · A DB reverse fly is heaviest at the top, exactly where the rear delt is shortest and weakest

items.name: Incline DB Curl
items.note: 60 sec rest · Shoulder extended puts the long head in its lengthened position · 3 sec eccentric, no body English

items.name: Landmine Rotation
items.note: 60 sec rest · Transverse plane · Hip-to-shoulder sequence, driven from the ground · Velocity is the point — add load only every 3–4 weeks

days.label: PUSH
days.notes: Three pressing angles, then position work. The cable and cam picks aren't preference — a dumbbell is heaviest where the delt and pec are already shortened, which caps how much you can actually load them there.

items.name: Band Pull-Aparts
items.note: Frontal · Scapular retraction · Rear delt counterbalance before pressing

items.name: DB External Rotation (side-lying)
items.note: Transverse · Elbow pinned at 90° · Light load · Pressing hides a rotation demand — this preps it

items.name: Bodyweight Dips
items.note: Sagittal push primer · Then ramp sets into Bench Press

items.name: Barbell Bench Press
items.note: 2–3 min rest · Raise the 1RM on the Strength page when you hit 6 across all 4 sets

items.name: Standing Overhead Press
items.note: 2 min rest · Build from the bottom of the range, earn the top

items.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
items.note: 2 min rest · Hit 6 across all 4 to earn the next load

items.name: Incline DB Press
items.note: 90 sec rest · Pec in its lengthened position · Stop short of lockout so tension never leaves the top

items.name: Pec Deck
items.note: 60 sec rest · Pec shortened · Cam corrects what a DB fly can't — a dumbbell is nearly weightless at the squeeze

items.name: Cable Lateral Raise (low pulley, across body)
items.note: 60 sec rest · Cable across the body holds tension through the whole arc · A DB raise peaks at the top, where the delt is already shortened

items.name: Overhead Cable Extension
items.note: 60 sec rest · Long head only reaches its stretch with the shoulder flexed · Cable over skull crusher — the barbell goes light exactly where you're most stretched

days.label: LEGS
days.notes: Squat is the primary mover. RDL trains hip extension with the hamstring lengthened, the seated curl trains knee flexion from that same lengthened position — both hamstring jobs, every session.

items.name: Feet-Elevated Side Crunch
items.note: Frontal · Neutral push-up → lateral flexion → back to neutral

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.note: Transverse · Hip internal and external rotation under control

items.name: Hip CARs
items.note: Transverse · Full hip circle, slow · Then ramp sets into Squat

items.name: Back Squat or Safety Bar Squat
items.note: 2–3 min rest · Two days clear of deadlift so neither lift is run on the other's fatigue

items.name: Romanian Deadlift
items.note: 2 min rest · Pattern over load · Hamstring lengthened at the hip — this is hip extension, not knee flexion

items.name: Hack Squat
items.note: 90 sec rest · Loads the quad deep in its lengthened position · Fixed path drops the balance tax the squat already charged you

items.name: Leg Extension
items.note: 60 sec rest · Quad shortened · Cam matches the strength curve where no free weight can

items.name: Seated Leg Curl
items.note: 60 sec rest · Hip flexed leaves the hamstring fully lengthened before the curl · Seated, not lying — the lying version trains the shortened end instead

items.name: Hip Thrust or Cable Pull-Through
items.note: 60 sec rest · Glute shortened · Pairs with the RDL's lengthened position for full curve coverage

items.name: Cable Pallof Press
items.note: 60 sec rest · Anti-rotation · Resist the rotation before you train producing it · Ribs down, hips square
